subject: Request: proof of patch velocity & CVE rollback process
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@greenline.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@greenline.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: proof of patch velocity & CVE rollback process

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Security asked us to collect some concrete evidence before we move the integration into our staging environment. Two asks they flagged as urgent:

1) Patch velocity: a short cadence summary (past 90 days) showing average time-to-patch for critical/important CVEs and the SLA commitments you track.
2) Rollback / mitigation process: if a patch causes a regression, what is the documented rollback process + how quickly you can revert to a known-good model or runtime? They specifically asked for an attestation we can include in our vendor review packet.

Can you share a single packet or point me to a Drive folder with the scan summaries, an attestation statement, and the rollback playbook? We need this by next Wednesday (29 Sep) to keep our procurement timeline.

Appreciate it — Samir

[External attachment: Greenline-Vendor-VM-Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@greenline.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: proof of patch velocity & CVE rollback process

Samir,

Thanks — we can get that to you. Quick overview inline and we'll attach a compact packet:

- Patch velocity: we publish a quarterly "patch rhythm" spreadsheet that shows median time-to-patch for Critical/High/Medium over rolling 90-day windows, plus the distribution of fix vs. compensating-control outcomes. For Q3 2027 medians: Critical = 7 days, High = 21 days, Medium = 45 days.

- SLAs: for Dedicated customers we commit to <72h for critical CVEs when a vendor patch is available; for Hosted we operate on a best-effort with automated mitigation & accelerated rollouts — we provide documented exceptions in the packet.

- Rollback: we maintain an automated deployment system with immutable model + serving image tags. Rollback sequence is: 1) flag incident in PagerDuty, 2) trigger automatic canary revert to last-known-stable image (<10 minutes to initiate), 3) if revert fails, route traffic to warm standby in alternate region while we troubleshoot. The attached "cve-rollback-playbook-v2.pdf" contains timelines and owners.

Attachments included: redwood_patch_rhythm_q3-2027.xlsx; cve-rollback-playbook-v2.pdf; sept-kv-scan-summary-2027.pdf (scan summary that maps to the patch table).

We'll also add a signed attestation paragraph at the front of the packet that you can drop into your vendor binder. If you want a separate notarized letter, let us know.

Rishi
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_patch_rhythm_q3-2027.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: cve-rollback-playbook-v2.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: sept-kv-scan-summary-2027.pdf (pdf)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@greenline.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: proof of patch velocity & CVE rollback process

Samir — adding a couple of operational details so your reviewers have the context they usually ask for:

- Scan cadence: internal authenticated infrastructure scans run daily; external-facing surface scans run weekly. We run credentialed container/image scans on every build pipeline and surface findings into our VM backlog (Jira project VM) where owners are auto-assigned.
- Evidence linkage: the spreadsheet includes references to the specific scan runs (see column "scan_run_id"); the sept summary includes sample findings and closure timestamps.
- Verification: we can run a short proof run with your security team on a sample CVE (non-prod) to show patch-to-verify timeline; typical verification completes inside the SLA windows above.

Jonas, can you confirm the stated median times are consistent with our ticketing exports? If you can attach an export snippet from VM-4892 that would be great.

Thanks,
Monica
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: none]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@greenline.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: proof of patch velocity & CVE rollback process

Hi all — I pulled the export and validated the numbers. Confirming details for your packet:

- Export sample: Jira VM-4892 export (CSV snippet) attached — it shows created -> resolved timestamps for high & critical issues over July–Sept. Median resolution (created to resolved) for Critical = 7d, High = 20d.
- Rollback playbook: the playbook includes a runbook for canary revert with step-by-step commands and the automated job name; typical revert to previous image is <10 minutes to take effect, and rolling back a model variant across a full cluster is usually completed in under 30 minutes with automated health checks.
- Attestation: Rishi, I added a short attestation clause at the front of the PDF saying: "Redwood attests that the attached patch cadence and rollback processes reflect our production practice as of 2027-09-29; we commit to notify customers of any material changes in the process within 7 days."

Samir — everything is in Drive here: https://drive.redwood.com/Greenline/VM-evidence-q3-2027. The three files previously listed are in the folder. If you need a signed/transmittal PDF for procurement, let me know and I will route to Legal.

Best,
Jonas
Security Engineering
